# Diagnosing a Go specification-running command-line tool without a test suite

This is a command-line tool for writing tests as readable prose files and running them against code that lives in a separate child process, and it now gets a great deal of that wrong. Nothing about the file syntax changed and nothing about the projects being run changed. The repository has received 30 separate undocumented edits. What follows is everything that has been noticed from the outside, arranged by what someone was doing at the time.

Tidying a written file into its canonical shape damages two things. The line of tags comes back carrying its separating comma after the last tag and omitting it between the earlier ones, so three tags run together with a stray comma trailing them. Line breaks on action lines are handled backwards too: a line whose text already ends in a newline gets a further marker and newline appended, while an ordinary line loses its break and is welded onto whatever follows it.

Opening those files and turning them into something runnable goes wrong in several ways. A trailing after-everything section that holds nothing but a table has that table's heading line filed as one of the section's own action lines instead of being left as the plain text it is, so the section comes back carrying a step that was never written in it.
